q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration _____.
e: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration g. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as _____ fall.
e: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall. By definition that quantity is free.

q: In free fall equations, we use the symbol h for displacement s and g for acceleration _____.
e: In free fall equations, we use the symbol h for displacement s and g for acceleration a. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The first equation of motion for free fall is v = v₀ + _____.
e: The first equation of motion for free fall is v = v₀ + gt. The physics in this sentence is built around gt.

q: The second equation of motion for free fall is v² = v₀² + _____, where h is the height.
e: The second equation of motion for free fall is v² = v₀² + 2gh, where h is the height. The physics in this sentence is built around 2gh.

q: The third equation of motion for free fall is h = v₀t + _____gt².
e: The third equation of motion for free fall is h = v₀t + 1/2gt². The physics in this sentence is built around 1/2.

q: The acceleration due to gravity g is directed _____ (towards the centre of the earth).
e: The acceleration due to gravity g is directed downwards (towards the centre of the earth). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The value of g varies only slightly from one place to another, and therefore, its value is assumed to be _____ in the calculations.
e: The value of g varies only slightly from one place to another, and therefore, its value is assumed to be constant in the calculations. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: In solving free fall problems, displacement h will be positive if it is _____ the origin and negative below the origin.
e: In solving free fall problems, displacement h will be positive if it is above the origin and negative below the origin. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: In free fall problems, velocities v₀ and v will be positive if they are directed upward and negative if directed _____.
e: In free fall problems, velocities v₀ and v will be positive if they are directed upward and negative if directed downward. The physics in this sentence is built around downward.

q: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards, its value will be negative (i.e. g = _____ m s⁻²).
e: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards, its value will be negative (i.e. g = -9.8 m s⁻²). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.
